Here is a detailed **7-Day China Trip Itinerary** following the classic "Golden Triangle" route — **Beijing → Xi'an → Shanghai** — which is widely regarded as the best option for first-time visitors!

---

# 🇨🇳 7-Day China Trip Itinerary: The Golden Triangle

The most popular week-long route for first-timers is the Golden Triangle of **Beijing, Xi'an, and Shanghai**. These three cities cover the cultural essentials: the Great Wall and Forbidden City, the Terracotta Warriors, and China's modern skyline.

---

## 📅 Day 1 — Arrival in Beijing

- Fly into **Beijing Capital International Airport**.
- Take the Airport Express train to the city center for ¥25 — it's a better option than taxis during rush hour.
- Spend your evening walking through the vibrant **Dongcheng District**.
- Settle into your hotel and rest up for the days ahead.

---

## 📅 Day 2 — Explore Historic Beijing

- Start your day at **Tiananmen Square** around 7:30 AM before the crowds arrive. Head to **Jingshan Park** for excellent views of the Forbidden City. Later, explore the traditional hutongs around **Nanluoguxiang**.
- A trip to Beijing would not be complete without a visit to **The Forbidden City**, which houses one of the world's best collections of Chinese art, including traditional Chinese art from the Ming and Qing Dynasty, ancient halls, and objects of cultural and historical significance.
- In the evening, enjoy a traditional **Peking Duck dinner** in the city.

---

## 📅 Day 3 — The Great Wall & Summer Palace

- Visit the **Mutianyu section of the Great Wall** — it's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the Wall.
- After your half-day tour of the Great Wall, head to the **Summer Palace**, one of the most celebrated royal palaces of the Qing Dynasty. Built as an imperial garden, it served as a summer resort for Chinese Emperors.
- At night, take the **overnight train to Xi'an**.

---

## 📅 Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors & City Wall

- Arrive in Xi'an in the morning.
- Marvel at the world-renowned **Terracotta Army**, an extraordinary underground army guarding China's first emperor. Later, visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda**.
- An optional evening trip to **Great Tang All Day Mall** offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture.

---

## 📅 Day 5 — Xi'an City Wall & Travel to Shanghai

- **Ride a bike along the ancient Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. Afterward, travel to Shanghai.
- Don't miss a stroll through Xi'an's famous **Muslim Quarter** for street food and local culture before departing.
- Arrive in Shanghai in the evening and check in to your hotel.

---

## 📅 Day 6 — Shanghai: The Bund, Yu Garden & Skyline

- Stroll along **The Bund** to admire the striking skyline across the river. Then explore the classical beauty of **Yu Garden** and its bustling surrounding market.
- Wander through Yuyuan Bazaar and sample Shanghai's famous **xiaolongbao (soup dumplings)**.
- In the afternoon, take a leisurely stroll along **Nanjing Road** before heading back to The Bund, where colonial-era buildings blend seamlessly with futuristic skyscrapers.

---

## 📅 Day 7 — Shanghai: Museums & Departure

- Head to the **Shanghai Museum**, the best place to end your Shanghai adventure. It is known for its vast collection of historical and cultural items including traditional Chinese painting, calligraphy, ancient bronze ware, and ceramics from the Han, Tang, and Qing Dynasties.
- Explore more of Shanghai at your own pace, and don't forget to grab some souvenirs to remember your incredible trip!
- Head to the airport for your departure flight.

---

## 🧳 Essential Travel Tips

### 🛂 Visas
- China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations. A 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance.
- Visa policies update regularly, so confirm the latest requirements with your local Chinese embassy or consulate before booking.

### 🚄 Getting Around
- The railway system in China nearly covers the entire country, and the high-speed train is often the better choice, with trains reaching speeds of 200–350 km/h. High-speed rail stations are usually closer to city centers, and fares are generally more affordable and stable year-round.

### 📱 Technology & Apps
- Download and install at least two paid **VPNs** before you get on the plane, as once you land, you won't be able to access the app stores to download them.
- China's "Great Firewall" blocks access to Google, Gmail, Instagram, WhatsApp, and other Western apps — a VPN is your key to staying connected.
- Download and set up an app like **Alipay or WeChat Pay** before you arrive in China, as the country is largely cashless.
- Use **Amap** for navigation instead of Google Maps — it's in English, relatively user-friendly, available on Android, and far more accurate.

### 🌤️ Best Time to Visit
- In general, the best time to have decent weather in most parts of China is to visit in **May or October**.
- Be aware of major holidays: **Lunar New Year** (around February), **Labour Day** (late April/early May), and **Golden Week** (early October) — these are particularly crowded and expensive times to visit.

### 💰 Budget Expectations
- Budget travelers can expect to spend around **$30–50/day** (hostels, street food), mid-range travelers **$80–150/day** (hotels, restaurants, attractions), and luxury travelers **$200+/day** (5-star hotels, private tours).
